newsitem.title: USA: Junk debt issuance moderate, new high-grades firm.
newsitem.headline: Junk debt issuance moderate, new high-grades firm.

text.p: Moderate issuance in the U.S. high-yield bond market on Thursday was led by a $200 million offering from Venezuela's CANTV Finance Ltd, dealers said.
Investment grade issuance, meanwhile, will pale in comparison to Wednesday's $2.5 to $3 billion in volume, syndicates said. Most new issues were flat to firmer.

--General Motor's GMAC $1.0 billion global five-year notes were quoted unchanged from Wednesday's close at 41 bid-lock, traders said. The issue was priced at 42 basis points over the U.S. Treasury curve.
Merrill Lynch & Co Inc and J.P. Morgan Securities co-managed the GMAC global.
--GTE Corp $500 million 30-year debentures traded near the initial issue spread of 97.5 basis points. The deal was priced by a Goldman, Sachs & Co syndicate.

Investment grade issuance, beefed up by the three-month deluge of capital securities, has added up for one of the busiest January's in recent years, according to several seasoned syndicate members. That volume is expected to slow during the next two weeks, they added.
"This market has absorbed the supply surprisingly well and we think things will begin to let up going forward," one syndicate manager said. "Trust issues, for one, will subside."
For Thursday, PSE&G is expected to issue its trust preferred issue in the range of $100 million.

Back in the high-yield market, CANTV Finance Ltd issued $100 million 8.875 percent five-year notes to yield 260 basis points over the Treasury note. Another tranche of $100 million 9.25 percent notes due 2004 was priced to yield 285 basis points over the Treasury curve.
CANTV was more than five times oversubscribed with orders from a range of emerging markets, high-yield, crossover high-grade and European investors, according to the Chase Securities syndicate.

Other high-yield issues set to price on Thursday are $100 million senior subordinated notes from Vintage Petroleum Inc from Salomon Brothers in the 215 to 230 basis point range and $125 million senior notes from Advanced Radio Telecom Corp from Merrill Lynch.
